sections.h2: Where Elk County deeds are recorded
sections.html:
The Recorder of Deeds shares an office with the Register of Wills and the Clerk of Orphans' Court. Hand deliveries go to 250 Main Street, Ridgway, PA 15853. Mail goes to P.O. Box 314, Ridgway, PA 15853.

Ridgway is the county seat, and St. Marys is the largest city. If you live in St. Marys or Johnsonburg and mail a deed to Ridgway, allow time for delivery. Title companies usually skip the mail by using e-recording, and the office names Simplifile and CSC as its current partners.

The office records, protects and reproduces legal documents for Elk County real estate. It also collects realty transfer tax on behalf of the Commonwealth, the school districts and the municipalities. Records since 1843 are open to the public, except military discharges.

A standard deed costs $92.75 to record on the schedule that took effect December 1, 2025. The price covers four names, four pages and one parcel, and the schedule lists fees apart from state and local realty transfer tax.

Elk County recording fees by document
DocumentRecording fee
Deed or mortgage$92.75
Quit claim deed or easement$79.75
Satisfaction or release of mortgage$81.75
Assignment of mortgage$81.75
Sheriff's deed or correction deed$81.75
Tax claim deed$79.75
Power of attorney$18.50
UCC filing$100.00

Extra pages are $2.00 each, extra names are $0.50 each, and extra parcels on deed documents are $0.50 each. A subdivision or survey map 18 by 24 inches or smaller is $50.00, and a larger map is $62.50.

Credit and debit cards work through AllPaid for transactions that do not involve realty transfer tax or inheritance tax. AllPaid adds a convenience fee of 2.5% of the transaction, with a $3.99 minimum.

Title agents and do-it-yourself sellers both run into a short list of rules. Check your document against it before you send it.

  • Leave a 1-inch top margin on every page, because the office stamps recording data automatically.
  • Put the tax parcel identifier (UPI) on any instrument that affects land.
  • State the true consideration on every deed.
  • Pay state realty transfer tax with its own check or electronic payment.
  • Attach an original signed Statement of Value (REV-183) plus a copy if you claim an exemption from tax, unless the deed itself gives the reason.

If the property lies in more than one taxing jurisdiction, the person recording must give the percentage in each. Fees and taxes are due at recording, so the closing agent should bring payment with the package.

The recorder collects state and local realty transfer tax at recording. The state share goes on its own check, separate from the other fees.

Elk County's municipalities and school districts set their own local share, so the rate depends on where the house is. Ask the Recorder of Deeds for the combined rate for your township, borough or the city of St. Marys before you set a net-proceeds figure. The municipal list includes Benezette, Fox, Highland, Horton, Jay, Jones, Millstone, Ridgway and Spring Creek townships, along with Johnsonburg and Ridgway boroughs and St. Marys.

Heirs selling an inherited house deal with the same office, which issues letters and keeps wills. That helps when a deed cannot be signed until someone has authority to act for the estate.

Deeds from 1864 to the present can be searched online. Anything older has to be searched at the office. Guests can view records with some information redacted. An account with a credit card lets you save or print an unredacted copy at 50 cents per page, the same price as in the office.

Older books lettered A through Z need four zeros ahead of the letter in the search tool, for example 0000B. A live chat link to the software vendor is on the search page if the tool misbehaves.

  • Records open to inspection: since 1843, except military discharges
  • Online searchable: 1864 to present
  • Older than 1864: search in person at the office

The Register of Wills fee schedule effective December 1, 2025 shows what an estate pays before a house can be sold. Letters testamentary or of administration start at $76.25 for an estate not exceeding $1,000 and rise with the value of the estate. That fee includes the $41.25 judicial computer and access to justice surcharge.

  • Probate of a will only: $15.00 for the first page, $2.00 for each added page
  • Short certificates: $5.00 each
  • Certified copy of a will: $10.00 for the first 10 pages
  • Inheritance tax return filing: $15.00
  • Certification of inheritance tax paid, issuing: $15.00

Ask the Register of Wills which filings your estate needs. A buyer's title company will want letters in hand before it closes on a deed signed by an executor or administrator.

The county's population was estimated at 29,926 in July 2025, down 3.4% from the 2020 base. It has 16,968 housing units, and 79.5% of occupied homes are owner-occupied. The median home value for 2020 to 2024 is $133,600, and median gross rent is $719.

The assessment office has used a 50% ratio since the countywide reassessment of 2005, which took effect in 2006. Its example of total county, municipal and school mills is 16.15 for 2025 and 18.40 for 2026. Assessed value is therefore about half of market value, so do not compare your assessment directly with a sale price.

The usual sequence starts at closing, where you sign the deed before a notary. The title agent or attorney adds the UPI, states the true consideration, prepares the Statement of Value if one applies, and writes one check for recording fees and a separate one for state transfer tax. The package then goes to Ridgway by e-recording through Simplifile or CSC, or by courier or mail.

When you sell without a title company, call the office first and ask for the current fee and the local tax rate for your municipality. A cash sale needs the same deed, fees and tax, so allow the same lead time.

Keep your receipt and ask for a copy of the recorded deed. You can find the new record in the online search later, and if the search tool misbehaves, the chat link mentioned above reaches the software vendor. Questions about a rejected package go to the Ridgway office, where the staff can tell you which of the deed rules was missed and what the corrected package needs before it is brought back.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Elk County?
faqs.a: A deed costs $92.75 under the December 1, 2025 schedule, with four names, four pages and one parcel included. Extra pages are $2.00 each and extra names or parcels are $0.50 each.

faqs.q: Where is the Elk County Recorder of Deeds?
faqs.a: It is at 250 Main Street, Ridgway, PA 15853, in the office shared with the Register of Wills and Clerk of Orphans' Court. Mail goes to P.O. Box 314, Ridgway, PA 15853.
Yes. Simplifile and CSC are the current e-recording partners. Title companies usually submit seller deeds this way.

faqs.q: Can I pay Elk County recording fees by credit card?
faqs.a: Yes, for transactions that do not involve realty transfer tax or inheritance tax. AllPaid charges a convenience fee of 2.5% of the transaction, with a $3.99 minimum.

faqs.q: How far back do Elk County online deed records go?
faqs.a: Online deed search covers 1864 to the present. Deeds recorded before 1864 must be searched in the office.
